To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the spatial distribution of species richness is a complex function of environmental variables, (2) species richness is not always positively correlated with environmental variables, (3) species richness is a non-linear function of environmental variables and, (4) species richness is an interaction between environmental variables.
(a) the use of regression models for spatial predictions is a very powerful tool for biodiversity assessment and conservation management, and (b) the use of such models is not yet widespread.

(i) the spatial distribution of species richness can be predicted from a few environmental predictors, (ii) the accuracy of predictions is high, and (iii) spatially explicit predictions can be used to identify areas with high biodiversity value and areas that are likely to have a high conservation value.

the development of spatially explicit models for the prediction and assessment of species distributions, and for the evaluation of the effectiveness of conservation measures.
